sources.title: Simple return vs. Logarithmic return - additional aspects
sources.author: Motty Shai

examples: Original hypothetical examples; no market data. Prices in THB, returns in decimal unless labelled percent. No external cash flows, fees or taxes unless explicitly discussed.
editorial_checks: Compounding simple returns and summing log returns are equivalent after conversion.
Log conversion does not remove economic losses or establish Normality or backtest quality.
Exponentiating a log return produces gross return; subtract one for simple return.
The Simon Leung 100 to 120 example has exactly 20% cumulative return.
KS tests with fitted parameters require appropriate calibration.
